report:
Built place(items) in layout.py exactly as the owner's three steps say. I did not use helper.quick_layout.

Why not the helper: README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md say to always call helper.quick_layout. I read what it really does. It sorts items widest first, ignores each slot, and packs from x = 0. That breaks all three owner steps: x = slot, shift only on overlap with the previous item, keep the given order. It would also fail the existing test (a 0, b 5 would come back as a 0, b 1). So the owner's method wins here. A reviewer who follows CONTRIBUTING.md may object; that is the owner's call.

What the code does, step by step:
1. "Put each item at its given slot: x = slot." Each x starts at its slot.
2. "If an item overlaps the item before it, shift it right until it no longer overlaps that item." Walking in the given order, if x < previous_x + previous_width, x becomes previous_x + previous_width (the smallest shift that ends the overlap). previous_x is the previous item's x after its own shift.
3. "Return the list of (name, x), in the order the items were given." Done.

Results:
- Existing test: 1 passed (pytest).
- place([("a",0,3),("b",1,2),("c",6,1)]) gives a 0, b 3, c 6.
- place([("a",0,3),("b",1,2),("c",2,1)]) gives a 0, b 3, c 5.
- place([]) gives [].

Note: the overlap test x < previous_x + previous_width is also true for an item slotted left of the previous one, so it moves right too. As a result every item ends at or after the end of the one before it, and no two items overlap.

The unused import of quick_layout in layout.py is left as it was.
